1.75%（1.32 到 2.18）、上泌尿道尿路上皮癌 1.14%（0.77 到 1.52）、腎癌 1.05%（0.80 到 1.29）。族群標籤寫明是十六歲以上、因懷疑泌尿道癌被轉到二線照護、先前沒有泌尿科惡性腫瘤的人；旁邊一個警語盒寫這個分母是已經被轉到二線照護的人，不是所有驗到血尿的人，更不是一般人口，基層診所的分母完全不一樣。第二格是哪一種血尿：肉眼看得見的血尿是這份資料裡最強的單一標記，校正後勝算比 3.47（95% 信賴區間 2.90 到 4.15），並註明勝算比是兩組有比沒有的比值，不是機率差幾倍；下面三條橫條是比較好讀的絕對數字，來自指引引用的三千五百人以上前瞻觀察研究：肉眼血尿 13.2%、整體 10.0%、只有顯微血尿 3.1%。第三格是試紙：指引定義顯微血尿為一次適當採集的尿液、顯微鏡下每高倍視野超過三顆紅血球，並明文寫不應該只憑試紙陽性就定義為顯微血尿；兩條橫條是 237 位試紙陽性女性中 20.3% 鏡檢正常，以及 54 位只憑試紙轉診的人只有 26% 鏡檢真的陽性；旁註吃抗凝血劑或抗血小板藥不改變評估。第四格是這張圖的主軸：同樣是顯微血尿，三個驗證研究、三個分層的惡性率。低或可忽略風險那一組：第一份 1,018 人全做膀胱鏡加影像，低風險 218 人 0 例，是 0%；第二份 15,779 人全做膀胱鏡，低風險 727 人 3 例，是 0.4%；第三份 1,730 位女性，低風險 322 人 0 例，是 0%；這一層指引的建議是六個月內重做一次尿液檢查，不是立刻排膀胱鏡。中風險那一組：第一份 447 人 14 例，是 3.1%；第二份 1,863 人 18 例，是 1.0%；第三份 463 人，是 0.2%；建議是膀胱鏡加腎臟超音波。高風險那一組：第一份 353 人 20 例，是 5.7%；第二份 13,189 人 836 例，是 6.3%；第三份 945 人，是 1.3%；建議是膀胱鏡加軸狀上泌尿道影像，無禁忌時首選多期相尿路攝影。同一格裡有一個打上叉的空白方塊，寫著「這張圖沒有計分表」：沒有年齡、抽菸包年、血尿程度的打勾格，也沒有加總的分數，因為指引自己承認這套分層不完美——它把尿路上皮癌與其他泌尿道癌的風險混在一起算，用的卻主要是膀胱癌的風險因子。旁邊誠實補上另一半：1,018 人那份研究整體查到 34 個惡性（3.3%），其中 32 個（94%）是低惡性度的 Ta；查多了也有代價，指引自己列了膀胱鏡的不適與感染風險、顯影劑反應、輻射誘發癌症的可能與偽陽性引發的後續檢查。第五格是女性這一格，左右兩欄並列，中間是一條虛線，標明兩件事在同一份文件裡並存，這張圖不調和它們，中間不畫箭頭也不畫等號。左欄是路徑上的落差：從第一次血尿申報到確診，女性平均 85.4 天、男性 73.6 天（P 小於 0.001）；拖超過六個月的比例女 17.3%、男 14.1%；女性被診斷為泌尿道感染的勝算比 2.32（2.07 到 2.59）；接受腹部或骨盆影像的勝算比 0.80（0.71 到 0.89）；轉診前看過三次以上家醫的女男勝算比，膀胱癌 2.31（1.98 到 2.69），在 24 種癌裡性別效應最強；指引引用的存活落差是女性五年 73.3% 對男性 78.2%，措辭是「可能有一部分歸因於」診斷延遲。來源標籤寫明第一組是美國保險申報資料（2004 到 2010 年，男 5,416、女 2,233），第三組是英格蘭 2010 年全國癌症病人經驗調查（41,299 人、24 種癌）。右欄是同一份指引 2025 年的修訂：把女性的低風險年齡從五十歲以下放寬到六十歲以下、中風險改成六十歲以上，並明文寫女性不應該單憑年齡被歸類為高風險，理由是那份 1,730 位女性的資料裡 13 件惡性有 11 件在六十歲以上。第六格標題寫著「拖了就會變末期：這張圖上沒有那條箭頭」。四條橫條是 SEER-Medicare 29,740 人研究的校正風險比，拖到九個月才確診相對於三個月內確診者：整體 1.34、再校正期別與分化度後 1.29、低惡性度那一群 2.11、低期別 Ta 或 Tis 那一群 2.02，圖上並畫了一條 1.0 的參考虛線。說明寫著效應最強的地方是最不容易長進肌肉層的那兩群，這是未量測混雜的形狀；指引自己的措辭也只寫到這些延遲被認為可能促成 34% 的癌症特異死亡上升。下面補上另一份 1,384 位新診斷膀胱癌的多中心資料：顯微血尿者 T2 以上佔 11.6%、肉眼血尿者 17.9%，多變項勝算比 1.69（1.05 到 2.71，P 等於 0.03），但兩群人的分化度沒有差別，那是同一時間點上兩群人的期別分布差異，不是同一個人拖下去的後果。最後一句寫撐住「這個月就去查」的是另外兩根柱子：這個族群本來就有四分之一是膀胱癌，而查清楚它是一次門診檢查就有答案的事。第七格是沒有血尿的那一格：英國 NICE 的三款轉診門檻——四十五歲以上無法解釋且沒有泌尿道感染的肉眼血尿、感染治好後仍持續或復發的肉眼血尿、六十歲以上無法解釋的非肉眼血尿合併排尿痛或血檢白血球上升；另有一個淡色方塊寫六十歲以上反覆或持續且原因不明的泌尿道感染，考慮非緊急轉診。旁邊寫歐洲指引的原位癌可能在有下泌尿道症狀、特別是刺激性排尿症狀的病人身上被懷疑，以及美國指引要求血尿被歸因於泌尿道感染者治療後要再驗一次鏡檢。第八格是第一輪的三件事，三欄並排：膀胱鏡（有懷疑症狀時做，必要時切片；它不能被細胞學或任何其他非侵入性檢查取代）；上泌尿道影像（腎臟與膀胱超音波和／或電腦斷層尿路攝影；超音波無法排除上泌尿道尿路上皮癌，也不能取代電腦斷層尿路攝影）；尿液細胞學（膀胱鏡的輔助，高惡性度／G3 敏感度 84%、低惡性度／G1 只有 16%，陰性不能排除，至少 25 毫升新鮮尿、晨尿不適合）。下方一個虛線框寫著這一格不是通則：看到膀胱腫瘤就一定要做 CT 尿路攝影不是指引寫的，原文是在選定的情況下做，例如腫瘤長在三角區或多發、高風險的腫瘤，因為膀胱腫瘤病人的上泌尿道腫瘤發生率只有 1.8%，三角區才升到 7.5%。圖的最下面是台灣端：健保支付標準有 28019C 膀胱鏡檢查 1,800 點、15001C 體液細胞檢查 480 點（說明含尿液）；「CT 尿路攝影」在支付標準全文檔搜尋是零筆，查不到列項，要問醫務課或個管師，不往任何一邊推論；重大傷病證明有效期限五年；台灣血尿門診的癌症檢出率查不到官方統計。
en_alt: Schematic: how much the yield of investigation differs between kinds of blood in the urine and between groups of people. The first panel gives the denominator after referral to urology: IDENTIFY, a prospective cohort across 26 countries and 110 hospitals that recruited 10,896 people, found a urinary tract cancer in 28.2 per cent after adjustment for age, type of haematuria, sex, smoking, hospital and country, with a 95 per cent confidence interval of 22.3 to 34.1. Bars from longest to shortest read bladder cancer 24.7 per cent (19.1 to 30.2), prostate cancer 1.75 per cent (1.32 to 2.18), upper tract urothelial carcinoma 1.14 per cent (0.77 to 1.52) and kidney cancer 1.05 per cent (0.80 to 1.29). The population label states that these were people aged sixteen and over, referred to secondary care with suspected urinary tract cancer and with no previous urological malignancy, and a warning box adds that this denominator is people already referred to secondary care - not everyone with blood in the urine and certainly not the general population, the denominator in primary care being an entirely different one. The second panel is which kind of blood: visible haematuria is the strongest single marker in the dataset, adjusted odds ratio 3.47, 95 per cent confidence interval 2.90 to 4.15, with a note that an odds ratio is a ratio of odds between two groups rather than a multiple of the probability. Three bars below give the absolute numbers from a prospective observational study of more than 3,500 people quoted by the guideline: visible haematuria 13.2 per cent, overall 10.0 per cent, microhaematuria only 3.1 per cent. The third panel is the dipstick: the guideline defines microhaematuria as more than three red blood cells per high-power field on microscopic evaluation of a single, properly collected specimen, and states that it should not be defined by a positive dipstick alone; two bars show that 20.3 per cent of 237 women with a positive dipstick had normal microscopy, and that only 26 per cent of 54 people referred on the dipstick alone were confirmed on microscopy; a note adds that anticoagulant or antiplatelet treatment does not change the evaluation. The fourth panel is the axis of the figure: for the same microhaematuria, the malignancy rate in three validation studies across three risk groups. In the low or negligible risk group: the first study of 1,018 people, all of whom had cystoscopy and imaging, found 0 cancers among 218, that is 0 per cent; the second, of 15,779 people who all had cystoscopy, found 3 among 727, that is 0.4 per cent; the third, of 1,730 women, found 0 among 322, that is 0 per cent; and for this group the guideline recommends repeating the urine test within six months rather than going straight to cystoscopy. In the intermediate group: 14 cancers among 447, 3.1 per cent; 18 among 1,863, 1.0 per cent; and 0.2 per cent among 463 women; the recommendation is cystoscopy plus renal ultrasound. In the high-risk group: 20 cancers among 353, 5.7 per cent; 836 among 13,189, 6.3 per cent; and 1.3 per cent among 945 women; the recommendation is cystoscopy plus axial upper tract imaging, with multiphasic CT urography preferred where there is no contraindication. The same panel carries a hatched box crossed out and labelled "there is no scoring table in this figure": no boxes for age, pack-years or degree of haematuria and no total to add up, because the guideline itself concedes the system is imperfect - it groups the risk of urothelial cancer with that of other urological cancers while using risk factors that are chiefly those for bladder cancer. Beside it the other half is set down honestly: in the 1,018-person study 34 cancers were found in all, 3.3 per cent, and 32 of them, 94 per cent, were low-grade Ta; and investigating more has costs the guideline lists, namely the discomfort and infection risk of cystoscopy, contrast reactions, the possibility of radiation-induced cancer and false positives leading to further tests. The fifth panel is the cell for women, in two columns with a dashed rule between them labelled to say that both statements stand in the same document, that this figure does not reconcile them, and that there is no arrow and no equals sign between the columns. The left column is the gap in the pathway: from the first claim for haematuria to diagnosis, women waited 85.4 days on average against 73.6 days for men, P below 0.001; 17.3 per cent of women against 14.1 per cent of men waited longer than six months; the odds of being given a diagnosis of urinary tract infection were 2.32 (2.07 to 2.59) and the odds of undergoing abdominal or pelvic imaging 0.80 (0.71 to 0.89); the odds, women against men, of three or more GP consultations before referral were 2.31 (1.98 to 2.69) for bladder cancer, the strongest sex effect of the 24 cancers studied; and the survival gap quoted by the guideline is 73.3 per cent at five years in women against 78.2 per cent in men, with the wording "may be in part attributable to" delay in diagnosis. A source line records that the first set comes from United States claims data for 2004 to 2010, 5,416 men and 2,233 women, and the third from the 2010 National Cancer Patient Experience Survey in England, 41,299 people and 24 cancers. The right column is the 2025 amendment to the same guideline: the low-risk age threshold for women was relaxed from under fifty to under sixty and intermediate risk became sixty and over; it states that women should not be characterised as high risk on age alone; and the reason is that in the study of 1,730 women, 11 of the 13 cancers were in women aged sixty and over. The sixth panel is headed "leave it and it becomes advanced: that arrow is not on this figure". Four bars give adjusted hazard ratios from the SEER-Medicare study of 29,740 people, for diagnosis at nine months rather than within three: overall 1.34; after further adjustment for stage and grade 1.29; in the low-grade group 2.11; in the low-stage Ta or Tis group 2.02; a dashed reference line marks 1.0. The note explains that the effect is strongest in the two groups least likely to invade the muscle, which is the shape of unmeasured confounding, and that the guideline goes no further than saying these delays have been suggested to contribute to a 34 per cent increase in cancer-specific mortality. Below it a multicentre series of 1,384 newly diagnosed bladder cancers is added: 11.6 per cent of those presenting with microhaematuria were T2 or above against 17.9 per cent of those with visible haematuria, multivariable odds ratio 1.69 (1.05 to 2.71, P equals 0.03), but there was no difference in grade between the groups - a difference in the stage distribution of two groups at one moment in time, not what happens to one person who waits. The panel closes by noting that what does hold up going to get it checked this month are two other pillars: a quarter of this group turn out to have bladder cancer, and settling the question takes one clinic visit. The seventh panel is the cell with no blood in it: the three NICE referral thresholds - aged forty-five and over with unexplained visible haematuria without urinary tract infection; visible haematuria that persists or recurs after successful treatment of infection; aged sixty and over with unexplained non-visible haematuria and either dysuria or a raised white cell count - together with a pale box for considering a non-urgent referral in people aged sixty and over with recurrent or persistent and unexplained urinary tract infection. Alongside, the European guideline notes that carcinoma in situ might be suspected in patients with lower urinary tract symptoms, especially irritative voiding symptoms, and the American guideline asks for the urine to be examined again after treatment where haematuria was attributed to infection. The eighth panel sets out the first round of tests in three columns: cystoscopy, done where symptoms suggest bladder cancer, with biopsy where needed, and which cannot be replaced by cytology or any other non-invasive test; upper tract imaging, the initial work-up using renal and bladder ultrasound and/or CT urography, with ultrasound unable to exclude upper tract urothelial carcinoma and unable to replace CT urography; and urine cytology, an adjunct to cystoscopy with a sensitivity of 84 per cent for high-grade or G3 tumours and only 16 per cent for low-grade or G1, a negative result excluding nothing, and a specimen of at least 25 mL of fresh urine required, first morning urine being unsuitable. A dashed box below records that this cell is not a general rule: "once a bladder tumour is seen, CT urography must follow" is not what the guideline says - the sentence is that CT urography should be performed in selected cases, for example tumours in the trigone or multiple or high-risk tumours, because the incidence of upper tract tumours in people with a bladder tumour is only 1.8 per cent, rising to 7.5 per cent for the trigone. At the foot of the figure is the Taiwanese section: the National Health Insurance fee schedule lists 28019C, cystoscopy, at 1,800 points and 15001C, body fluid cytology, at 480 points with urine included in the description; a full-text search for "CT urography" returns nothing, so there is no line item to find and the billing office or case manager has to be asked, with nothing inferred either way; the catastrophic illness certificate is valid for five years; and no official statistics exist for the cancer detection rate of haematuria clinics in Taiwan.

en_alt: Schematic: three quality indicators for a first transurethral resection of a bladder tumour, when a second resection is indicated, and why blue light remains unsettled. Across the top are three cards holding the three checkable quality indicators. The first is whether there is detrusor muscle in the specimen: the guideline states that the absence of detrusor muscle is associated with a significantly higher risk of residual disease, early recurrence and tumour under-staging, and that its presence is considered a surrogate criterion of resection quality and is required, except in Ta low-grade / G1 tumours. The second is whether the resection was visibly complete: an incomplete initial resection, or doubt about completeness, is itself the first indication for doing it again, and if the report does not record whether the resection was visibly complete, that is a question to put. The third is whether the specimens were submitted separately labelled: specimens from different biopsies and resection fractions go to the pathologist in separately labelled containers, the tumour base is submitted separately, especially for large or multifocal tumours or where en-bloc resection is not feasible, and cauterisation is avoided as far as possible. Next come the numbers for the detrusor cell: recurrence at the first follow-up cystoscopy was 44.4 per cent where the specimen contained no muscle and 21.7 per cent where it did, and 67.7 per cent of specimens in the same cohort contained detrusor muscle. The population label gives a prospective Edinburgh cohort, n=356, of newly diagnosed patients whose resection was judged visibly complete at operation; the odds ratio is 2.9 (95 per cent confidence interval 1.6 to 5.4), P=0.0002; and a note adds that an odds ratio is a ratio of odds between two groups rather than a multiple of the probability, that both absolute numbers are given, and that the absolute numbers are what to read. The following panel is quality measured twice, in two columns. On the left, the Scottish national quality indicator programme: five-year recurrence was 38.9 per cent in hospitals meeting the detrusor sampling benchmark against 44.3 per cent in the rest, 5.4 percentage points lower (95 per cent confidence interval 1.6 to 9.2), P=0.005; the multivariable hazard ratio was 0.81 (0.73 to 0.91) and the progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.62 (0.45 to 0.84); the population was 2,688 patients with non-muscle-invasive disease among 3,899 newly diagnosed between April 2014 and March 2017, with a median follow-up of 60.3 months, and the programme had no national pre-implementation control group, making this an observational association. On the right, checklists against seniority, two datasets pointing opposite ways: the Edinburgh series found senior surgeons' specimens more often contained detrusor muscle, while a prospective collaborative database of 503 cases - 265 senior consultants, 149 junior consultants, 89 residents - found the opposite, residents' specimens containing detrusor muscle more often, odds ratio 1.75 (1.03 to 2.99), P=0.04; residents and junior consultants completed the surgical checklist more often, 56 per cent and 56 per cent against 44 per cent, P=0.009; and five-year recurrence-free survival was unrelated to seniority. Below the two columns a line records that what can be read out of this is that the checklist explains the difference better than seniority does, not that anyone resects better, and that the figure draws no ranking by seniority. The next panel is the second resection: three indications - an incomplete initial resection or doubt about completeness, no detrusor muscle in the initial specimen, and T1 tumours - two clearly marked exceptions, Ta low grade / G1 and primary CIS, and the timing, within two to six weeks of the initial resection and including the original tumour site, with retrospective data showing that resections done at 14 to 42 days gave better recurrence-free and progression-free survival than those at 43 to 90 days. Then what a second resection actually finds. Four bars come from a meta-analysis in T1 disease (29 studies; 3,566 patients for residual disease and 2,556 for upstaging): residual tumour in all patients 0.56 (95 per cent confidence interval 0.48 to 0.63); upstaging to muscle invasion in all patients 0.10 (0.06 to 0.14); residual tumour 0.47 in the 1,565 whose first specimen already contained muscle; and upstaging still 0.10 in that subgroup, marked as no lower. A line is picked out beside them: "there was muscle this time" does not mean "no second resection is needed". Below, a second systematic review (31 studies, 8,409 patients with high-grade Ta and T1 disease) gives ranges: residual tumour 17 to 67 per cent for Ta and 20 to 71 per cent for T1, with most residual disease, 36 to 86 per cent, at the original resection site; upstaging from Ta to T1 or above 0 to 8 per cent, and from T1 to T2 or above 0 to 32 per cent. Contemporary numbers are lower: in an updated meta-analysis of 81 studies, T1 patients treated by conventional resection in the 2010s had any residual disease in 31.4 per cent (26.0 to 37.2) and upstaging in 2.8 per cent (2.0 to 3.8), with a warning of potential publication bias. The size of the benefit is set down honestly: after adjustment, recurrence-free survival hazard ratio 0.78 (0.62 to 0.97) and overall survival 0.86 (0.81 to 0.93) were better, but progression-free survival 0.74 (0.47 to 1.15) and cancer-specific survival 0.94 (0.86 to 1.03) showed no difference. The panel closes with the guideline's counter-example: in one single-centre series 104 of 209 patients with high-grade Ta disease had a second resection and only 1 was upstaged to T1, none to T2 or above, while the patients for whom the guideline indicated a second resection had significantly worse recurrence-free and progression-free survival - the shape of selection bias. The next panel is en-bloc resection: the phase 3 randomised trial that met its primary endpoint (multicentre, Hong Kong; 350 randomised, 276 pathologically confirmed non-muscle-invasive, tumours 3 cm or less) gave one-year recurrence of 29 per cent (95 per cent confidence interval 18 to 37) against 38 per cent (28 to 46) for standard resection, P=0.007; one-year progression 0 per cent against 2.6 per cent (0 to 5.5), P=0.065; detrusor sampling and the other secondary endpoints similar in the two arms; and median operating time 28 against 22 minutes. A note records that two further randomised trials found no difference in time to recurrence, so what can be said is that at 3 cm or less, with one-year recurrence as the endpoint, one trial saw a difference - not that en-bloc resection is better - and that this figure draws no ranking of techniques. The penultimate panel is blue light, carrying a red status pill reading "unsettled", in two columns with "seeing more clearly is not the same as recurring less" between them and no arrow. On the left, detection: patient-level sensitivity 92 per cent for blue light against 71 per cent for white light, biopsy-level 93 per cent against 65 per cent, at the cost of lower specificity, 63 per cent against 81 per cent, with inflammation, a recent resection and the three months after BCG instillation all capable of causing false positives. On the right, recurrence: in the PHOTO randomised trial the three-year recurrence hazard ratio was 0.94 (0.69 to 1.28), P=0.70; the three-year recurrence-free rate 57.8 per cent against 61.6 per cent; and the cost £876 more over three years with no difference in quality-adjusted life years; the population was 22 hospitals in the United Kingdom, 538 randomised and 426 in the primary analysis, in newly diagnosed intermediate and high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease. A footnote records that the two randomised trials of narrow-band imaging were also negative overall with a signal only in a low-risk subgroup, and that the guideline goes no further than a weak recommendation - use methods to improve tumour visualisation during resection, if available - while writing that further investigation is needed. The last panel lists the seven lines that should appear on the pathology report: tumour location, grade, stage, lymphovascular invasion, subtypes of urothelial carcinoma, presence of CIS and detrusor muscle; with a small box beside it noting that where cytology is positive but cystoscopy shows nothing, the guideline asks that upper tract urothelial carcinoma, CIS in the bladder and tumour in the prostatic urethra all be excluded. At the foot of the figure is the Taiwanese section: the fee schedule lists 78008C, endoscopic resection of a bladder tumour including cystoscopy, at 8,027 points, the first note reading that a cystoscopy report must accompany the claim; bladder instillation is 50011C at 260 points; of the 3,809 bladder cancers in the Taiwan Cancer Registry long-form report for 2023, 1,630 (42.79 per cent) had resection combined with intravesical chemotherapy and 558 (14.65 per cent) resection alone; a full-text search for "blue light", "photodynamic", "narrow-band imaging" and "en-bloc resection" returns nothing, so the billing office or case manager has to be asked and nothing is inferred either way; and whether Taiwan has surgical quality indicators of the Scottish kind, or how often second resections are done, cannot be established from official statistics.

侵犯淺層肌肉（內半）、T2b 侵犯深層肌肉（外半）；再往外是膀胱周圍組織，標 T3a 顯微可見、T3b 肉眼可見的膀胱外腫塊；最外層是鄰近器官，標 T4a 攝護腺基質、精囊、子宮或陰道，T4b 骨盆壁或腹壁。剖面下方註明版本：UICC 的 TNM 第 9 版在 2025 年出版，但官方版本異動總表上膀胱那一列全部標示無異動，所以這些定義第 8 版跟第 9 版一樣；台灣癌症登記 112 年報告的整併期別明載依 AJCC 第 8 版。中間是兩張並排的卡片，講這條線決定什麼。左邊那張標「非肌肉侵犯型」：Ta、Tis、T1 都可以用經尿道刮除處理，因此為了治療目的被歸在非肌肉侵犯型膀胱癌這個標題之下；指引自己補了一句，這個詞代表的是一個群體定義，所有腫瘤仍應依期別、分化度與其他病理特徵各自描述，它是一個為了決定治療而畫的框，不是一個診斷；分到哪一層風險、要不要灌藥是另一篇。右邊那張標「肌肉侵犯型」：T2 以上要在切除膀胱與保留膀胱之間選路；分化度那一行不看了，因為膀胱的肌肉侵犯型尿路上皮癌全部都是高惡性度，分化度無法提供預後資訊。兩張卡片下方有一行：指引有一條強度較高的建議寫著不要使用「淺層」膀胱癌這個詞，理由是因為它不正確，T1 已經長進固有層，一點也不淺。再往下是一整格標題為「登記表上的期別欄位，不是這條線」的區塊。上面是一條 100% 堆疊長條，畫的是美國 SEER 的期別欄位（SEER 21 不含 IL，2016 到 2022 年）：原位 50%、五年相對存活 98.0%；局限 34%、73.0%；區域 7%、41.8%；遠端 6%、9.6%；不詳 3%。長條上用一個括弧標出「局限」那一段，寫著它同時裝著 T1（沒有侵犯肌肉）與 T2（已經侵犯肌肉）。旁邊的說明是：這兩群人的治療路徑完全不同，所以「膀胱癌五年存活 73%」這種句子是把線兩邊的人混在一起講，等於沒有講；台灣自己的膀胱癌五年存活率，癌症登記中心公布的存活分析只涵蓋十大癌症，膀胱癌不在裡面，查不到官方數字。接下來是台灣的分布：癌症登記長表 112 年（2023 診斷年）膀胱癌 3,809 例，整併期別依 AJCC 第 8 版，0 期 38.08%、I 期 34.68%、II 期 13.06%、III 期 9.37%、IV 期 4.82%，上方括出 0 期加 I 期等於 72.8%（線的左邊）、II 到 IV 期等於 27.2%（線的右邊），分母 3,737，另有 72 例不詳。旁註 0 期那一格要拆開看，Ta 有 1,321 例、Tis 只有 102 例。同一區塊有一個警語盒：台灣有兩個官方的膀胱癌年度數字，不可互換也不可相減——長期趨勢檔 2023 年 2,562 例（男 1,826、女 736），檔案自己註明此為侵襲癌發生率數據；長表統計同年 3,809 例，包含原位癌 1,452 例（38.1%）與侵襲癌 2,357 例。再下面是 CIS 的獨立方塊，分左右兩欄。左欄是指引定義逐字：一種上皮內的、高惡性度的、非侵入性尿路上皮癌；如果沒有切片，膀胱鏡下可能被漏掉或被誤判為發炎病灶；常常是多發的，可以長在膀胱，也可以長在上泌尿道、攝護腺導管與尿道；臨床上分原發、續發、併發三型。左欄下方有一條紅字：CIS 的診斷無法單靠影像方法做出，電腦斷層尿路攝影、靜脈注射尿路攝影、超音波，包括多參數磁振造影在內都不行，只能靠切片。右欄是它把人放到哪一格：除了很高風險那一類，所有 CIS 病人都歸在高風險；原發的純 CIS 視為高風險；攝護腺尿道的 CIS 屬於很高風險。接著是分化度的兩套寫法，左欄 1973 年那套寫 G1、G2、G3，右欄 2004 年以後那套寫 PUNLMP、低惡性度、高惡性度，兩欄中間是一條虛線，標明中間沒有箭頭、沒有等號、也沒有換算表。下方說明：兩套系統之間病人在類別之間有顯著的移動，2004/2022 版的高惡性度人數增加，因為它納入了一部分預後比 G3 好的 G2 病人；指引小組的系統性回顧寫得最白——G1 病人的惡化率與低惡性度病人相近，G3 病人的惡化率則高於高惡性度病人。再下面是混合四層的五年惡化率橫條：低惡性度／G1 是 1.4%、低惡性度／G2 是 3.8%、高惡性度／G2 是 7.7%、高惡性度／G3 是 18.8%，資料來自 17 個中心、1990 到 2019 年、5,145 位原發 Ta／T1 病人，64% 是 Ta，中位追蹤 3.9 年，log-rank P 小於 0.001；預測惡化的 C 指數 1973 那套 0.71、2004 那套 0.67、兩套合起來 0.73；兩套系統對復發都沒有預測價值，有價值的是對惡化。再下一格是報告本身的不確定性，三條橫條：CIS 的診斷一致率 70 到 78%、T1 對 Ta 的分期判讀 50 到 60%、分化度判讀 50 到 60%；旁註這不是誰不認真，是這幾個判斷本來就在灰帶，指引因此寫在 T1 以上或困難的案例，可以考慮由有經驗的泌尿生殖病理醫師再看一次。倒數第二格講變異型與淋巴血管侵犯：2022 年世界衛生組織分類把所有變異型都視為高惡性度；非肌肉侵犯型病人中最多有 14.6% 帶有變異型，高惡性度成分超過 5% 就算高惡性度腫瘤；會把人推到很高風險那一格的包括純微乳頭、肉瘤樣、巢狀、漿細胞樣與神經內分泌型，以及合併 CIS、淋巴血管侵犯、多發、殘存腫瘤或不完全刮除。圖的最下面是一個金框方塊：台灣 112 年 3,809 例膀胱癌中，侵襲癌 2,357 例裡泌尿上皮癌佔 95.59%，另有神經內分泌癌 30 例、腺癌 36 例、鱗狀細胞癌 10 例，組織型不同時治療邏輯會整個換一套；這張圖能替你做的只有一件事，是把報告上的字換成可以問出口的問題：我的 T 是哪一個、在肌肉層這條線的哪一邊、分化度用的是哪一套系統、有沒有寫 CIS、變異型與淋巴血管侵犯、我拿到的是臨床期別還是病理期別。
en_alt: Schematic: Ta, Tis, T1 and T2-and-above on a bladder cancer report are the two sides of one line, drawn in the muscle layer of the bladder wall. The upper half of the figure is a cross-section of the bladder wall in five layers from the inside out. The urothelium, or mucosa, carries Ta, non-invasive papillary carcinoma, and Tis, carcinoma in situ, a flat tumour. The lamina propria, the subepithelial connective tissue, carries T1, tumour invades subepithelial connective tissue. Then comes a thick line labelled "the first line: the muscle layer". Below it the muscle layer, the detrusor, carries T2a, invasion of superficial muscle or inner half, and T2b, invasion of deep muscle or outer half. Outside that the perivesical tissue carries T3a, microscopically, and T3b, macroscopically, an extravesical mass. The outermost layer, adjacent organs, carries T4a, prostate stroma, seminal vesicles, uterus or vagina, and T4b, pelvic wall or abdominal wall. A note under the cross-section records that the UICC TNM 9th edition was published in 2025 but that every bladder column in the official table of changes is marked unchanged, so these definitions are the same in the 8th and 9th editions, and that the Taiwan Cancer Registry report for 2023 states its collapsed stage follows AJCC 8th edition. In the middle are two cards side by side showing what the line decides. The left card, tagged non-muscle-invasive, says that Ta, Tis and T1 can all be treated by transurethral resection and are therefore grouped, for the purposes of treatment, under the heading of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer; that the guideline adds that this term represents a group definition and that every tumour should still be described by stage, grade and other pathological features, making it a frame drawn to decide treatment rather than a diagnosis; and that which risk group a person falls into, and whether anything is instilled, belongs to another article. The right card, tagged muscle-invasive, says that from T2 upwards a route has to be chosen between removing the bladder and keeping it, and that the grade line is no longer read, because all muscle-invasive urothelial carcinomas of the bladder are high grade and grading therefore provides no prognostic information. Below the two cards a line records that the guideline strongly recommends not using the term "superficial" bladder cancer, the reason given being "because it is incorrect": T1 has already grown into the lamina propria and is not superficial at all. Next comes a panel headed "the stage field in a registry is not this line". At the top is a single full-width stacked bar of the SEER stage field, SEER 21 excluding Illinois, 2016 to 2022: in situ 50 per cent with five-year relative survival 98.0 per cent; localised 34 per cent with 73.0 per cent; regional 7 per cent with 41.8 per cent; distant 6 per cent with 9.6 per cent; unknown 3 per cent. A bracket marks the localised segment and reads: this cell holds T1, with no muscle invasion, and T2, with muscle invaded, at the same time. The note beside it explains that those two groups follow completely different treatment pathways, so a sentence such as "bladder cancer has a five-year survival of 73 per cent" averages the two sides of the line together and amounts to saying nothing; and that for Taiwan no official five-year survival exists at all, because the registry's published survival analysis covers only the ten commonest cancers and bladder cancer is not among them. The Taiwanese distribution follows: the Taiwan Cancer Registry long-form report for year 112, diagnosis year 2023, recorded 3,809 bladder cancers, with collapsed stage by AJCC 8th edition - stage 0 38.08 per cent, stage I 34.68 per cent, stage II 13.06 per cent, stage III 9.37 per cent and stage IV 4.82 per cent - bracketed above as stage 0 plus stage I equals 72.8 per cent, on the left of the line, and stages II to IV equal 27.2 per cent, on the right, over a denominator of 3,737 with a further 72 cases unknown. A note adds that the stage 0 cell must be opened up, because it holds 1,321 cases of Ta and only 102 of Tis. The same panel carries a warning box: Taiwan publishes two official annual counts that are not interchangeable and must never be subtracted from one another - the long-term trend file gives 2,562 cases for 2023, 1,826 men and 736 women, and notes that this is the incidence of invasive cancer, while the long-form report for the same year gives 3,809, including 1,452 carcinomas in situ, 38.1 per cent, alongside 2,357 invasive cancers. Below this is a panel on CIS in two columns. On the left, the guideline definition word for word: an intra-epithelial, high-grade, non-invasive urothelial carcinoma; if it is not biopsied it can be missed at cystoscopy or misinterpreted as an inflammatory lesion; it is often multifocal and can arise in the bladder but also in the upper urinary tract, the prostatic ducts and the urethra; and clinically it comes as primary, secondary or concurrent disease. A red line underneath states that a diagnosis of CIS cannot be made by imaging alone - not CT urography, intravenous urography or ultrasound, and not multiparametric MRI either - so CIS needs a biopsy. On the right, where it puts a person: apart from the very-high-risk group, every patient with CIS falls in the high-risk group; primary CIS alone is high risk; CIS of the prostatic urethra is very high risk. Next, grade written two ways: the left column, the 1973 system, reads G1, G2, G3; the right column, the system from 2004 onwards, reads PUNLMP, low grade, high grade; and the dashed rule between them is labelled to say there is no arrow, no equals sign and no conversion table. The explanation below records that there is a significant shift of patients between the categories of the two systems, the number of high-grade patients under 2004/2022 rising because that category takes in a subset of G2 patients with a better prognosis than G3, and that the panel's systematic review puts it most bluntly: progression rates in G1 patients are similar to those in low-grade patients, while progression rates in G3 patients are higher than in high-grade patients. Then four horizontal bars give five-year progression under the hybrid of the two systems: low grade / G1 1.4 per cent, low grade / G2 3.8 per cent, high grade / G2 7.7 per cent, high grade / G3 18.8 per cent, from 17 centres, 1990 to 2019, 5,145 patients with primary Ta or T1 disease, 64 per cent Ta, median follow-up 3.9 years, log-rank P below 0.001; the C-index for predicting progression is 0.71 for the 1973 system, 0.67 for the 2004 system and 0.73 for the two combined, and neither system predicts recurrence - what they predict is progression. The next panel is the uncertainty in the words themselves, as three bars: agreement on a diagnosis of CIS 70 to 78 per cent; staging T1 against Ta 50 to 60 per cent; reading the grade 50 to 60 per cent. The note says this is not carelessness but a grey zone by nature, and that the guideline therefore adds that in stage T1 and above, or in difficult cases, an additional review by an experienced genitourinary pathologist can be considered. The penultimate panel covers subtypes and lymphovascular invasion: the 2022 World Health Organization classification treats all subtypes as high grade; up to 14.6 per cent of non-muscle-invasive tumours harbour a subtype and more than 5 per cent high-grade component makes it a high-grade tumour; and the features that push a person into the very-high-risk group include pure micropapillary, sarcomatoid, nested, plasmacytoid and neuroendocrine subtypes, along with concurrent CIS, lymphovascular invasion, multiple tumours, residual tumour or an incomplete resection. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel records that of the 3,809 bladder cancers registered in Taiwan in 2023 the 2,357 invasive ones were 95.59 per cent urothelial carcinoma, with 30 neuroendocrine carcinomas, 36 adenocarcinomas and 10 squamous cell carcinomas, and that a different histological type means an entirely different treatment logic; and that the one thing this figure can do is turn the words on the report into questions that can be asked out loud - which T am I and which side of the muscle line does that put me on, which grading system does my report use, does it mention CIS, a subtype or lymphovascular invasion, and is the stage I have been given the clinical one or the pathological one.

試驗上；族群以接受膀胱灌注化療者為主；算出來的五年復發機率從 31% 到 78%，五年進展機率從不到 1% 到 45%；2026 年版的建議強度是 Strong，用於預測沒有用卡介苗的人的復發。右欄是 2021 年的 EAU 模型，問的是會不會往肌肉層長：只預測進展，終點是進展到肌肉侵犯或遠端轉移的時間；建立在 3,401 位病人的個別資料上；族群全部是初發的非肌肉侵犯型、1990 到 2018 年間治療、只收接受經尿道刮除加或不加膀胱灌注化療的人，接受輔助性卡介苗的人被排除在外；作者自列的限制是回溯性收案、沒有中央病理複閱；2026 年版的建議強度同樣是 Strong。兩欄下方寫著用了卡介苗的人另外有 2016 年的 EORTC 模型或 CUETO 模型，「新表取代舊表」這句話是錯的。第二格是這張圖的核心，標題是「同一格裡的兩個數字：極高風險的五年進展」。同一個座標軸上畫兩條：沒有接受卡介苗的那一條是 40%，95% 信賴區間 29% 到 54%，來自表 6.3；給了足量卡介苗之後的那一條畫成一段區間，14.9% 到 22%，來自同一份指引在極高風險的治療段落。說明寫著表 6.3 自己在表下註明這些百分比指的是初次刮除後沒有立刻接受輔助性卡介苗灌注的病人，所以 40% 是沒打卡介苗的一群人的平均，不是你的機率。分母標籤是 n 等於 3,401、全部初發、1990 到 2018 年治療、只做刮除加或不加灌注化療、排除接受輔助性卡介苗者，終點是進展到肌肉侵犯或遠端轉移的時間；同一群人的十年進展機率是 53%。旁邊一格寫日本一個 3,024 人的卡介苗治療世代拿 2021 模型去驗證，對進展的 C-index 只有 0.617（2019 年版是 0.572，p 等於 0.011）；C-index 翻成白話是隨便挑兩個人，模型能不能把先出事的那一個排在前面，0.5 是丟銅板、1 是全對；而且在這個世代裡，五個極高風險次組之間的存活曲線沒有顯著差異。第三格畫的是分層算出來的東西，不是輸入：四張卡片依序是低風險、中風險、高風險、極高風險。低風險那張：五年進展機率 0.93%（信賴區間 0.49% 到 1.7%）、十年 3.7%、五年復發機率 10% 到 35%；處置是術後單次即刻灌注化療，指引寫「對這些病人已經是足夠的治療」；並附上那一次灌注的雙面——11 篇研究、2,278 位 pTa–pT1 病人的個別病人資料統合分析（單純刮除 1,161 人對刮除加單次灌注 1,117 人），復發風險下降 35%（風險比 0.65，95% 信賴區間 0.58 到 0.74），五年復發率從 58.8% 降到 44.8%；但在過去每年復發超過一次或 2006 EORTC 復發分數 5 分以上的人身上沒有效，不延長到進展的時間、也不延長到膀胱癌死亡的時間，而且在高復發風險者身上整體死亡風險反而上升（風險比 1.26，95% 信賴區間 1.05 到 1.51，p 等於 0.015；五年死亡率 12.0% 對 11.2%）；反過來，低風險也不是卡介苗的對象，TICE 卡介苗美國仿單的使用限制欄自己寫不建議用於 TaG1 乳突狀腫瘤，除非被判斷為高復發風險。中風險那張：十年進展機率 7.4% 與 8.5%（兩套分級系統各一個）、五年復發機率 18% 到 50%；第一線多半是誘導期的膀胱灌注化療，加或不加最多一年的維持，一年份的全劑量卡介苗是替代選項；並寫明中風險在定義上就是「沒有原位癌，而且不落在低、高、極高任何一格」的其餘的人，國際膀胱癌小組 2022 年修訂的次分層模型在 677 人身上驗證，零個風險因子的人進展風險接近低風險、三個以上的人接近高風險，被歸在中風險不代表你在這個箱子的中間。高風險那張只寫一句：這一格的處置本篇正文沒有展開，灌的如果是卡介苗，那是完全另一回事，見〈卡介苗不是化療，也不是打疫苗〉。極高風險那張：五年進展機率（未接受卡介苗）40%、十年 53%；指引寫的是應與病人討論立即膀胱全切除，不是應該切；同一節也寫膀胱全切除從腫瘤學角度是最安全的做法，但伴隨併發症與生活品質的損失，對一部分病人而言是過度治療；原位癌無法靠內視鏡處置治癒，回溯資料裡灌注化療的完全反應率 48%、卡介苗 72% 到 93%，而完全反應的人當中最多一半日後仍然會復發；把非肌肉侵犯型直接讀成早期、不用擔心，是這一格最常被誤會的地方。第四格是一個打上叉的空白方塊，寫著「這裡沒有計分表」：沒有風險因子的勾選格、沒有切點，也沒有加總的分數。旁邊列出三個理由：第一，模型本身就沒有納入原發的純原位癌、攝護腺尿道原位癌、復發性腫瘤、變異型組織與淋巴血管侵犯；第二，各國指引的分層本來就不一樣，一篇 2022 年的綜論寫各國指引對低、中、高風險的歸類略有不同，歐洲用四層、美國那邊是三層，而美國泌尿科醫學會與泌尿腫瘤學會 2026 年的更新也再次調整了風險分層；第三，分層的前提是第一次刮除刮乾淨、檢體裡有肌肉層、必要時再刮一次，那一格不在你手上，在病理報告和刮除紀錄裡。同一格另有兩段：2026 年的指引新增第 10 章，標題是「Pragmatic deintensification strategy in NMIBC」，前提寫在同一段，建立在與充分知情並同意的病人共同決策的過程，減量是被討論出來的，不是自己決定少來幾次；同一章提到一個用 14 個臨床病理變項建立的人工智慧模型 PROGRxN-BCa，指引給它的評語是「Pending further validation」，在驗證完成之前不是現行標準。圖的最下面是一個金框方塊：同一個極高風險的 40%，在沒有打卡介苗的人身上和在打了足量卡介苗的人身上是兩個不同的數字，醫師指給你看的那一個是哪一種值得當場弄清楚，這一句問下去，40% 跟 14.9% 到 22% 的差別就出來了；錢的部分可以先問一半，膀胱灌注這個處置在健保醫療服務給付項目裡有列項（50011C，260 點），但灌進去的藥怎麼算是另一回事，要問醫院的醫務課或個管師。
en_alt: Schematic: the two risk models in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer set side by side, and the two numbers in the very-high-risk cell that have to be read together. The first panel holds the two questions and the two tables, with a dashed rule between them stating that the tables answer two different questions and that no arrow is drawn between them: recurrence is something appearing again on the same floor, progression is drilling down into the muscle. The left column is the 2006 EORTC tables, asking whether the disease will come back: the endpoint predicted is recurrence, with progression given too; they are built on 2,596 patients from seven EORTC trials; the population was mainly patients who received intravesical chemotherapy; the range produced is five-year recurrence of 31 to 78 per cent and five-year progression from under 1 per cent to 45 per cent; and the 2026 guideline grades the recommendation Strong, for predicting recurrence in people who have not had BCG. The right column is the 2021 EAU model, asking whether the disease will grow into the muscle: it predicts progression only, the endpoint being time to muscle invasion or distant metastasis; it is built on individual data from 3,401 patients; the population is all primary non-muscle-invasive disease treated between 1990 and 2018, taking only patients who had transurethral resection with or without intravesical chemotherapy, with those given adjuvant BCG excluded; the limitations the authors list are retrospective recruitment and no central pathology review; and the 2026 recommendation is likewise graded Strong. Below the two columns a line records that for people who have had BCG there are other models, the 2016 EORTC model and the CUETO model, and that "the new table has replaced the old one" is simply wrong. The second panel is the core of the figure, headed "two numbers in one cell: five-year progression in the very-high-risk group". On one scale two bars are drawn: without BCG, 40 per cent, 95 per cent confidence interval 29 to 54, from table 6.3; and after adequate BCG, drawn as a band from 14.9 to 22 per cent, from the treatment section for very high risk in the same guideline. The note explains that table 6.3 states beneath itself that these percentages refer to patients who were not immediately treated with adjuvant BCG instillations after their primary resection, so 40 per cent is the average of a group of people who did not have BCG and is not "your probability". The denominator labels are n equal to 3,401, all primary disease, treated between 1990 and 2018, resection with or without intravesical chemotherapy only, patients given adjuvant BCG excluded, with time to muscle invasion or distant metastasis as the endpoint; ten-year progression in the same group is 53 per cent. Beside it a panel records that a Japanese cohort of 3,024 BCG-treated patients tested the 2021 model and found a C-index for progression of only 0.617, against 0.572 for the 2019 version, p equal to 0.011; that a C-index asks whether the model can put the person who runs into trouble first ahead of the other for any two people picked at random, 0.5 being a coin toss and 1 perfect; and that in that cohort the survival curves of the five very-high-risk subgroups did not differ significantly. The third panel draws what the stratification produces rather than what goes into it, as four cards: low risk, intermediate risk, high risk and very high risk. The low-risk card gives five-year progression of 0.93 per cent (confidence interval 0.49 to 1.7 per cent), ten-year progression 3.7 per cent and five-year recurrence 10 to 35 per cent, with a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy after resection described by the guideline as sufficient treatment in these patients; and it sets out both sides of that instillation - an individual patient data meta-analysis of 11 studies and 2,278 patients with pTa-pT1 disease, 1,161 resection alone against 1,117 resection plus a single instillation, in which recurrence risk fell by 35 per cent, hazard ratio 0.65, 95 per cent confidence interval 0.58 to 0.74, and five-year recurrence fell from 58.8 per cent to 44.8 per cent; while in people with more than one recurrence a year, or a 2006 EORTC recurrence score of 5 or above, it had no effect, it lengthened neither time to progression nor time to death from bladder cancer, and in those at high risk of recurrence overall mortality rose, hazard ratio 1.26, 95 per cent confidence interval 1.05 to 1.51, p equal to 0.015, with five-year mortality 12.0 per cent against 11.2 per cent; and in the other direction, that the US TICE BCG label states BCG is not recommended for stage TaG1 papillary tumours unless they are judged to be at high risk of recurrence. The intermediate-risk card gives ten-year progression of 7.4 and 8.5 per cent, one figure from each grading system, and five-year recurrence of 18 to 50 per cent, with first-line treatment usually a course of intravesical chemotherapy with or without maintenance for up to a year and a year of full-dose BCG as an alternative; and it records that intermediate risk means everyone left over, with no carcinoma in situ and not falling into the low, high or very-high groups, and that the International Bladder Cancer Group's 2022 revision, validated in 677 patients, put people with none of the risk factors close to the low-risk group and people with three or more close to the high-risk group, so being placed in the intermediate group does not mean being in the middle of the box. The high-risk card carries one line only: the treatment for this group is not set out in this article, and if what is instilled is BCG that is an entirely different matter, covered in "BCG is not chemotherapy, and not a vaccination". The very-high-risk card gives five-year progression without BCG of 40 per cent and ten-year progression of 53 per cent, and records that the guideline says immediate radical cystectomy should be discussed with the patient rather than that it should be done; that the same section calls radical cystectomy the safest approach from an oncological point of view while noting that it brings complications and a loss of quality of life and represents over-treatment in some patients; that carcinoma in situ cannot be cured by endoscopic management, with complete response rates in retrospective data of 48 per cent for intravesical chemotherapy and 72 to 93 per cent for BCG, up to half of complete responders relapsing later; and that reading non-muscle-invasive as "early, nothing to worry about" is the mistake most often made in this cell. The fourth panel is a hatched box crossed out and labelled "there is no scoring table here": no boxes for risk factors, no cut-points and no total to add up. Three reasons stand beside it. First, the model itself leaves out primary carcinoma in situ on its own, carcinoma in situ of the prostatic urethra, recurrent tumours, subtype histology and lymphovascular invasion. Second, national guidelines stratify differently: a 2022 review states that international guidelines differ slightly in how they categorise low, intermediate and high risk, Europe using four groups and the United States three, with the 2026 AUA/SUO update adjusting its stratification again. Third, stratification assumes a complete first resection, detrusor muscle in the specimen and a second resection where indicated - and that cell is not in your hands but in the pathology report and the operation note. The same panel adds two further paragraphs: the 2026 guideline gained a chapter 10 headed "Pragmatic deintensification strategy in NMIBC", whose precondition is written into the same paragraph, namely a shared decision-making process in fully informed and consenting patients, so that doing less is arrived at in conversation rather than decided alone; and the same chapter mentions PROGRxN-BCa, an artificial intelligence model built on 14 clinicopathological variables including second resection and BCG treatment, on which the guideline's verdict is "pending further validation", meaning it is not the current standard. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel reads: the same 40 per cent for very high risk means one thing in people who never had BCG and another in people who had an adequate course of it, so which of the two your doctor is pointing at is worth settling on the spot - ask, and the difference between 40 per cent and 14.9 to 22 per cent comes out; and half of the money question can be answered too, since bladder instillation is a listed item in the National Health Insurance fee schedule, 50011C at 260 points, while how the drug instilled is accounted for is a separate matter for the hospital's billing office or your case manager.

en_alt: Schematic in three panels. The first, "the shape of a course: six weeks is only the beginning", draws a timeline: a six-week induction, one instillation a week, then maintenance with three weekly instillations again at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months, up to 27 in all; a note says the length of a course is not a score, and that who is given BCG and how often is decided by risk stratification. Below the timeline are two evidence cards. SWOG 8507 is a randomised trial: 660 patients had the six-week induction, 550 were randomised at three months to maintenance or none, and the primary analysis set was the 384 patients disease-free at randomisation; median recurrence-free survival was 35.7 months without maintenance against 76.8 months with it, p less than 0.0001; median worsening-free survival 111.5 months against not reached; five-year overall survival 78% against 83%. The card records that the authors themselves noted patients with bad side effects simply stopped maintenance, so the trial could not see severe toxicity. The second card is EORTC 30962, a randomised 2x2 trial (one-third dose or full dose, by one year or three years) in intermediate- and high-risk Ta and T1 disease, 1,355 patients in the intention-to-treat set, median follow-up 7.1 years: in high-risk patients two extra years reduced recurrence (hazard ratio 1.61, 95% confidence interval 1.13 to 2.30, p=0.009) but only at full dose; at intermediate risk two extra years at full dose bought nothing; progression and survival did not differ across the four arms. The second panel, "the days after an instillation, and how many people get through the course", shows a three-step timeline: bladder irritation begins 4 to 6 hours after instillation, lasts 24 to 72 hours, and is usually only marked after the third instillation; about 60% of patients get bladder irritation. The adverse-event table in the label, 674 patients including 153 with carcinoma in situ: painful urination 60% (grade 3 or worse 11%), urinary frequency 40% (7%), flu-like syndrome 33% (9%), fever 20% (8%). Completion: the guideline states more than half of patients cannot complete one year of maintenance, and in the three-year maintenance arm of EORTC 30962 only 34% completed the whole course. The same panel lists three things often mistaken for a contraindication which are not - white cells on the urine dipstick, invisible haematuria, asymptomatic bacteriuria - and the group that really has to wait, quoting the label verbatim: "Treatment should be postponed for at least 1 week following transurethral resection, biopsy, traumatic catheterization, or gross hematuria"; the guideline advises at least two weeks after a resection, and the contraindications section separately lists immunosuppression and active tuberculosis. The third panel is a red box, "what means going back the same day, rather than waiting for the next visit", listing verbatim the four signals the label calls suggestive of systemic BCG infection: flu-like fever lasting more than 72 hours; a fever reaching 103°F (about 39.4°C), or a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F) or above lasting more than two to three days; systemic symptoms getting worse with each instillation, or persistently abnormal liver blood tests; local acute inflammation - prostatitis, epididymitis, orchitis - lasting more than two to three days. Above the red box the label is quoted: "Deaths have been reported as a result of systemic BCG infection and sepsis.", together with the label's other sentence that malaise, fever and chills lasting one to two days usually reflect a hypersensitivity reaction. Below it: there is only one thing for you to do - go back the same day and say clearly which day the last instillation was; stopping the drug, cultures, imaging and referral are the clinical side, and the guideline's threshold is a persistent fever above 38.5°C for more than 48 hours, at which point BCG is stopped permanently. Three rates close the panel: serious side effects in fewer than 5% of patients, systemic BCG infection 1% to 2%, and among 5,033 exposed people in the Swedish national database a five-year cumulative notified tuberculosis diagnosis rate of 1.1%. The figure ends by stating that it is not a tool for deciding whether your own case is serious enough; that judgement belongs to the person who can see your results.

en_alt: Schematic comparing the follow-up schedules of the two roads in two columns. The left column is non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (Ta / T1 / CIS) under the EAU 2026 guideline; every recommendation carries the strength Weak and the guideline itself notes a lack of RCTs. One cell is not stratified: the first cystoscopy is always three months after TURBT, level of evidence 1a. Low risk: month 3, month 12, then yearly, with a stopping point after five years; the wording is "should be considered", not "stop". This stratum has no urinary cytology and no routine imaging, and a negative haematuria dipstick has negative predictive values of 0.89 and 0.94. Intermediate risk excluding high grade: month 3, six-monthly for two years, then yearly, with a stopping point after ten years; the high-grade subgroup within intermediate risk is followed as high risk. High and very high risk: three-monthly for two years, six-monthly to five years, then yearly, marked life long with no stopping point, because "Recurrences after ten years tumour-free are not unusual"; cytology runs at the same frequency as cystoscopy. High and very high risk carries a second axis, upper-tract CT urography: yearly to five years, two-yearly to ten years, also life long with no stopping point. The ten-year rate of upper-tract tumour ranges from 1.9% in T1 tumours to 25% in multiple recurrent high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, and reached 3.6% within ten years for high-risk patients (Ta G3 and CIS) in a population-based study. The right column is the bladder kept after trimodality therapy: three guidelines, three schedules, all three ending with no stopping point. EAU 2026: three-monthly cystoscopy for two years, six-monthly to year five, yearly thereafter, with cytology and chest, abdominal and pelvic CT or MRI including the upper tract every six to twelve months for the first three to five years. AUA / ASCO / SUO: three-monthly in year one, every four to six months in year two, every six to twelve months thereafter, with imaging six-monthly for the first two years and the guideline noting that no published data show that this frequency improves survival. NICE guideline NG2: rigid cystoscopy three months after radiotherapy, three-monthly for two years, six-monthly for the next two years, yearly thereafter, with upper-tract imaging yearly for five years. The intervals differ but all three end at "yearly thereafter"; not one reaches a stop. Two Taiwan lines at the foot: National Health Insurance item 28019C, cystoscopy, 1,800 points; and no entry found for any cap on the number of cystoscopies in follow-up, where zero hits means no entry was found rather than "not reimbursed", so ask the hospital medical affairs office or your case manager. Three closing questions: which stratum am I in or which guideline schedule am I on, does my schedule have a stopping point, and do I need upper-tract CT every year.

人，配對後五年總存活切除 62.6% 對三聯療法 36.7%；偏差在登記資料看不到的欄位裡——國際多中心的 RISC 世代量過，走保留那條路的人比較老、體能狀態比較差、共病比較多，三項 p 值都小於 0.01。第三支箭也指向右邊：Robesti 2025 重建 6 篇研究、8,594 人的存活曲線，12 個報告終點裡有 10 個存在追蹤中斷的不平衡（informative censoring），整體偏向膀胱切除；而校正之後膀胱切除仍然較優，五年總存活 42% 對 30%。圖上註明這一格對「保留膀胱做得太少」這個主張不利，所以一定要在圖上。第五格是生活品質：兩家醫院的橫斷面回溯研究，226 位兩條路都適合、無病存活至少兩年的人，回覆率 77%，173 人（三聯療法 64、切除 109），中位追蹤 5.6 年；傾向分數校正後三聯療法組的整體生活品質高 9.7 分（滿分 100，p=0.001）、性功能高 8.7 到 32.1 分、身體形象高 14.8 分，排尿症狀分數兩組相似；作者自己寫兩條路的長期生活品質都不錯，是不是比較好需要前瞻研究驗證，而兩組從診斷到填問卷還差了兩年。最後一格列出三句不准的讀法：「保留膀胱＝次等選擇」「保留膀胱＝一樣好」「不用開刀＝比較輕鬆」，各附一句理由；並揭露畫圖者的利益關係（三聯療法裡的放射治療是他自己在做的那一段），說明第三支箭與挽救性切除那一格都沒有被縮小；最後引 EAU「For all suitable candidates, both bladder-preserving techniques and RC should be discussed」與 NICE NG2 第 1.5.5 條「Offer a choice of radical cystectomy or radiotherapy with a radiosensitiser」，並寫明這張圖給的是要問醫師的問題，不是一個答案。
en_alt: Schematic putting the two roads in muscle-invasive bladder cancer - radical cystectomy and trimodality therapy (resection plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy) - on one table, with every cell carrying its study design, population, follow-up and number of patients. The top of the figure states that there is no successfully completed randomised trial on this question, quoting the EAU 2026 guideline verbatim: "No successfully completed RCTs are available comparing the outcomes of TMT with RC." Two cards follow. SPARE was a randomised feasibility study: first patient 20 July 2007, accrual closed 12 February 2010 on the advice of the independent data monitoring committee and the trial steering committee, with only 45 patients in all; of 796 screened patients with T2-T3 N0M0 disease 490 were ineligible, 165 were approached and 45 consented (27%), and of the 120 who declined, 51 preferred radiotherapy and 25 preferred surgery. The second card is DAVECA 8201 from 1991: a randomised trial, 183 patients, T2 to T4a, recruited 1983 to 1986, but it compared preoperative radiotherapy of 40 Gy plus planned cystectomy against radical radiotherapy of 60 Gy with cystectomy only for residual tumour, without concurrent chemotherapy - so it is not the trimodality therapy meant today. The second panel is Zlotta 2023: retrospective, propensity score matched and inverse-probability weighted, not a randomised trial; clinical T2-T4 N0M0 disease, 2005 to 2017, 722 patients (440 cystectomy, 282 trimodality therapy), median follow-up 4.4 and 4.9 years. The entry criteria are boxed separately: a solitary tumour under 7 cm, no hydronephrosis or unilateral only, no extensive or multifocal carcinoma in situ; and those 440 cystectomy patients were only 29% of all radical cystectomies done over the same period. The matched results are set side by side: five-year metastasis-free survival 74% against 74%, five-year cancer-specific survival 83% against 85% (p=0.057), five-year disease-free survival 76% against 76%; underneath, the figure states that this can only be read as "in this selected group of patients, these endpoints could not be told apart", and that not being able to tell them apart is not the same as being equally good. The third panel sets out what each road carries. For radical cystectomy: the EAU gives a strong recommendation in T2-T4a N0M0 disease, and on this operation alone about half of patients live beyond five years; 90-day mortality varies with the cohort - 2.5% in a selected university-centre cohort, 4.7% pooled across 66 retrospective studies, 5.6% in the Dutch national registry of 9,287 patients, and in the randomised SWOG S1011 trial 7% (19/292) in the extended lymph node dissection arm against 2% (7/300) in the standard arm; 90-day complications pooled 58.5% (36.1% to 80.5%); and people who have surgery get a pathological stage, of those 440, 44% pT3-4 and 26% node positive. For trimodality therapy: radiotherapy is 64 Gy in 32 fractions over six and a half weeks or 55 Gy in 20 fractions over four weeks with concurrent radiosensitising chemotherapy; in the randomised phase II RTOG 0712 trial treatment-related grade 3-4 toxicity was 21/33 (64%) in one arm and 18/33 (55%) in the other, and the meta-analysis of matched cohorts pooled acute grade 3 or worse toxicity at 11.4%; salvage cystectomy pooled across 73 studies and 9,110 patients followed beyond five years runs at about 19.2%, roughly one person in five, with an EAU modern-series range of 10% to 30% and a complication rate for that operation of 67% to 72%; none of the three guidelines gives a stopping point for cystoscopy after treatment, and quoting BC2001 patient-reported data the EAU records that about one third still score bladder symptoms below baseline at five years; people who keep the bladder only ever have a clinical stage. The fourth panel draws selection bias as three arrows, with "makes trimodality therapy look better" at the left end and "makes radical cystectomy look better" at the right. The first arrow points left: a meta-analysis restricted to matched cohort studies, 87 studies and 28,218 patients, overall survival hazard ratio 1.05 (95% confidence interval 0.78-1.40) and cancer-specific survival 1.05 (0.69-1.58), no difference detectable, the bias being that trimodality patients in single-centre and matched cohorts are selected, motivated and have favourable tumours, while the authors still call for evidence from high-quality controlled trials. The second arrow points right: NCDB 2004 to 2013, AJCC stage II to III, 32,300 patients, hazard ratio for death after matching 1.406 (1.235-1.601); SEER 2010 to 2022, T2N0M0, 10,495 patients, five-year overall survival after matching 62.6% with cystectomy against 36.7% with trimodality therapy; the bias sits in fields a registry cannot see - the international multicentre RISC cohort measured it, and people taking the preservation road were older, had worse performance status and more comorbidity, all three with p below 0.01. The third arrow also points right: Robesti 2025 reconstructed the survival curves of 6 studies and 8,594 patients and found that 10 of 12 reported endpoints carried an imbalance in dropping out of follow-up (informative censoring), overall favouring cystectomy, and that after correction cystectomy was still superior, with five-year overall survival 42% against 30%. The figure notes that this cell cuts against the claim that too little bladder preservation is being done, which is why it has to be shown. The fifth panel is quality of life: a cross-sectional retrospective study at two hospitals, 226 people suitable for either road and disease-free for at least two years, response rate 77%, 173 replies (64 trimodality therapy, 109 cystectomy), median follow-up 5.6 years; after propensity score adjustment the trimodality group scored 9.7 points higher on global quality of life (out of 100, p=0.001), 8.7 to 32.1 points higher on sexual function and 14.8 points higher on body image, with similar urinary symptom scores; the authors themselves conclude that long-term quality of life is good on both roads and that whether trimodality therapy is better needs prospective study, and the two groups were two years apart between diagnosis and questionnaire. The last panel lists three readings that are not allowed - "bladder preservation is the second-best option", "bladder preservation is just as good", "no operation means an easier time" - each with its reason; discloses that the person who drew the figure does the radiotherapy half of trimodality therapy himself, and that the third arrow and the salvage cystectomy cell have not been made smaller; and closes with the EAU line "For all suitable candidates, both bladder-preserving techniques and RC should be discussed" and NICE NG2 1.5.5 "Offer a choice of radical cystectomy or radiotherapy with a radiosensitiser", stating that what the figure gives is questions to ask your doctors, not an answer.

zh_alt: 示意圖，畫三種尿路改道的日子，三欄平列、順序不代表優劣。圖的最上面是指引自己的兩句原文：「Randomised controlled trials comparing conduit diversion with neobladder or continent cutaneous diversion have not been performed.」與「Currently, it is not possible to recommend a particular type of urinary diversion.」——沒有隨機試驗比較過三種改道，指引因此無法推薦其中任何一種；EAU 同時寫改道的方式不影響腫瘤結果，NICE 的措辭是選擇膀胱全切除的人要提供尿路造口或禁尿型改道，除非有認知功能障礙、腎功能受損或明顯腸道疾病這類強烈禁忌。第一欄是迴腸導管（肚皮上一個造口接尿袋）：EAU 形容它是「結果可預期」的成熟做法；30 天併發症 48%，以泌尿道感染、腎盂腎炎、輸尿管與迴腸接合處漏或狹窄為主；長期造口相關併發症最高到 24%；上泌尿道功能或形態變化最高到 30%；而它的晚期併發症在三種做法裡最少；要學的是造口與尿袋的照顧。第二欄是原位新膀胱（用腸子做一個袋子接回尿道，靠腹壓與放鬆括約肌排尿）：荷蘭、德國、西班牙的登記資料顯示男女各約一到兩成的人做這個；EAU 表列的新膀胱相關問題發生率 30% 到 64%；男性的前瞻評估顯示日間禁尿從術後三個月內的 59% 升到 12 到 18 個月時的 92%，夜間從 28% 升到 18 到 36 個月時的 51%；56 位女性新膀胱病人日間禁尿 70.4%、夜間 64.8%，但排空困難在女性特別常見——約三分之二需要自行導尿、將近 45% 完全無法自行排尿；要學的是定時排尿與（部分人）自行導尿。第三欄是輸尿管皮膚吻合（輸尿管直接接到肚皮）：EAU 寫它是最簡單的皮膚改道，手術時間、併發症率、失血、輸血率、加護病房停留與住院天數都比迴腸導管低；代價是輸尿管口徑小，造口狹窄與上行性泌尿道感染比用腸子做的造口多；對體弱者、或只有一顆腎而需要上泌尿道改道的人，它是首選；要學的是造口照顧以及導管更換的節奏。三欄底下標明：三欄的數字不是同一把尺——一欄報的是 30 天併發症，一欄報的是幾年後的禁尿率，一欄報的是跟另一種做法相比低的項目，它們不能互相相減，也不能排名。接著一格寫三段讀完會發現的事：最不像原本膀胱的那一種，晚期併發症最少；最像原本膀胱的那一種，夜間禁尿到一年半以上還只有一半；最簡單的那一種，是某些人的首選，而不是將就；所以這不是排名，是三組不同的日子。再下一格是長期的那張帳，三種做法一起算、不分欄：3,360 位因肌肉侵犯型膀胱癌接受膀胱全切除的人，29% 在 12 個月內進展到晚期慢性腎病；良性的輸尿管與腸道接合處狹窄最高到 20%；做腸道改道的人維生素 B12 偏低的比例 17%，EAU 建議每年驗一次；SEER 資料顯示膀胱全切除與骨折風險上升 21% 相關，推測與長期代謝性酸中毒和骨質流失有關，那是相關不是已經證明的因果；改道相關併發症在追蹤的前五年會偵測到 45%，一個 131 人的系列裡活過 15 年的人上升到 94%，15 年追蹤時 50% 出現上泌尿道變化、38% 有尿路結石；另有一份 1,383 人的回溯資料顯示迴腸導管與原位新膀胱在腎絲球過濾率下降的風險上沒有顯著差異，真正跟下降相關的是年齡與接合處狹窄。再下一格列出不必等下一次回診的訊號（沒有可引用的量化門檻，所以寫的是症狀不是數字）：發燒合併單側腰痛；造口的尿量突然變少或整天沒有尿；傷口或造口周圍一直滲出液體；做了新膀胱卻解不出尿而且腹脹——出現任何一樣，當天就聯絡手術團隊或回急診。同一格寫「怎麼選」比「選哪一種」更重要：EAU 記了讓病人在充分被告知之後做出改道的決定，與術後較少的決策後悔相關，而且「independent of the method selected」，跟最後選了哪一種無關；NICE 要求造口護理師在手術前後都要能談。最後一格列出兩句不准的讀法：「這三種有高下之分」與「照這張圖我就知道要選哪一種」。
en_alt: Schematic showing what the days look like with each of the three urinary diversions, in three columns set out flat, the order carrying no ranking. At the top are the guideline's own two sentences: "Randomised controlled trials comparing conduit diversion with neobladder or continent cutaneous diversion have not been performed." and "Currently, it is not possible to recommend a particular type of urinary diversion." - no randomised trial has compared the three, so the guideline cannot recommend any one of them; the EAU also records that the type of diversion does not affect the cancer outcome, and the NICE wording is that people choosing radical cystectomy should be offered either a urostomy or a continent diversion unless there is a strong contraindication such as impaired cognitive function, impaired renal function or significant bowel disease. The first column is the ileal conduit, a stoma on the abdominal wall draining into a bag: the EAU calls it a mature technique with predictable results; 30-day complications 48%, mostly urinary tract infection, pyelonephritis and leak or stricture at the ureteric and ileal anastomoses; long-term stoma-related complications up to 24%; functional or morphological change in the upper tract up to 30%; and its late complications are the fewest of the three; what has to be learnt is stoma and bag care. The second column is the orthotopic neobladder, a pouch built from bowel and joined back to the urethra, emptied by abdominal pressure and relaxing the sphincter: registry data from the Netherlands, Germany and Spain put its use at roughly one to two in ten of both men and women; the EAU tabulates neobladder-related problems at 30% to 64%; prospective assessment in men shows daytime continence rising from 59% within three months of surgery to 92% at 12 to 18 months, and night-time continence from 28% to 51% at 18 to 36 months; among 56 women with a neobladder, daytime continence was 70.4% and night-time 64.8%, but difficulty emptying is particularly common in women - about two-thirds need to self-catheterise and nearly 45% cannot void spontaneously at all; what has to be learnt is timed voiding and, for some, self-catheterisation. The third column is ureterocutaneostomy, the ureters brought directly to the abdominal wall: the EAU calls it the simplest form of cutaneous diversion, with operating time, complication rate, blood loss, transfusion rate, intensive care stay and days in hospital all lower than with an ileal conduit; the price is that the ureters are narrow, so stomal stenosis and ascending urinary tract infection are more common than with a stoma built from bowel; for frail patients, or for someone with a single kidney who needs upper tract diversion, it is the first choice; what has to be learnt is stoma care and the rhythm of catheter changes. Below the three columns the figure states that they are not one ruler: one reports 30-day complications, one reports continence rates years later, and one reports the items that are lower than with another technique, so they cannot be subtracted from one another and cannot be ranked. The next panel draws out what follows from reading all three: the one least like the original bladder has the fewest late complications; the one most like the original bladder still leaves only half of patients continent at night beyond a year and a half; the simplest one is some people's first choice, not a compromise; so this is not a ranking but three different sets of days. The panel after that is the long bill, counted for all three together in one column: among 3,360 people who had a radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer, 29% progressed to advanced chronic kidney disease within 12 months; benign ureteric-to-bowel anastomotic stricture up to 20%; vitamin B12 low in 17% of people with a bowel diversion, which the EAU advises checking once a year; SEER data associate radical cystectomy with a 21% higher fracture risk, thought to relate to long-term metabolic acidosis and bone loss, which is an association and not a proven cause; 45% of diversion-related complications are detected in the first five years of follow-up, rising to 94% among those surviving beyond 15 years in a series of 131 patients, with 50% showing upper tract change and 38% urinary stones at 15 years; and a retrospective dataset of 1,383 patients found no significant difference between an ileal conduit and an orthotopic neobladder in the risk of a falling glomerular filtration rate, what was actually associated with the fall being age and anastomotic stricture. The next panel lists the signals that do not wait for the next appointment - there is no citable quantitative threshold for any of them, so they are written as symptoms rather than numbers: fever with one-sided loin pain; a sudden fall in the volume draining from the stoma or no urine at all for a whole day; fluid leaking continuously from the wound or around the stoma; a neobladder that will not empty together with abdominal distension - if any of them appears, contact the surgical team or go to the emergency department the same day. The same panel records that how the choice is made matters more than which one is chosen: the EAU notes that a diversion decision made by a fully informed patient is associated with less decisional regret afterwards, "independent of the method selected", and NICE requires a stoma nurse to be available to talk both before and after the operation. The last panel lists two readings the figure must not be given: "one of the three is better than the others" and "now I know which one to pick".

zh_alt: 示意圖，把三份指引對「誰適合做三聯療法」的措辭並排成一張表：三欄分別是 EAU 2026、AUA／ASCO／SUO 2024 與 NICE NG2，六列分別是腫瘤數目與期別、原位癌、水腎、刮除、膀胱功能與病理型態。圖首先標明證據的形狀：拿三聯療法跟膀胱全切除比，沒有成功完成的隨機試驗，因收案不足收掉的那個試驗叫 SPARE，只收到 45 人，所以表裡的條件是指引的措辭，不是從隨機試驗算出來的門檻。EAU 那一欄逐字寫：腫瘤數目與期別是「solitary, unifocal cT2-T3a tumours」，原位癌是「absence of extensive or multifocal CIS」，水腎是「no or unilateral hydronephrosis」，刮除是做三聯療法時看得見的腫瘤要盡量刮掉、而且再刮一次超過一半的病例會發現殘餘病灶，膀胱功能是「good baseline bladder function」，病理型態則寫鱗狀、腺狀或微乳頭亞型的尿路上皮癌可以考慮，但純鱗狀細胞癌或腺癌應該建議直接手術；EAU 在同一段還寫了一句：患者篩選是拿到好結果的關鍵。AUA 那一欄逐字寫：「Patients with large tumors unable to be resected by TURBT, multifocal CIS, T3/T4 tumors, and/or hydronephrosis are not ideal candidates for any type of bladder preserving therapy.」原位癌那一格的理想人選寫成「no CIS」並建議做隨機切片去確認，水腎那一格寫成「no hydronephrosis」而且沒有「單側可以」那一句，刮除那一格寫成「complete resection is feasible」並以條文 22 要求最大程度的減積刮除，病理型態那一格寫腺癌、肉瘤與鱗狀細胞癌沒有被納入任何以放射線為主的保留膀胱前瞻研究；膀胱功能那一格畫成「—」，並註明「—」代表這張圖沒有從那一份文件引到對應的措辭，不代表那份指引對這一項沒有意見。NICE NG2 整欄以斜線網底畫成空白，並標明：這一欄是空的，NICE NG2 根本不給腫瘤條件，這一格是空的，不是漏抄，也不是還沒查到。表格下面另開一格寫 NICE 給的是程序而不是腫瘤條件：第 1.5.5 條「Offer a choice of radical cystectomy or radiotherapy with a radiosensitiser」；第 1.5.6 條要求討論時要有做膀胱全切除的泌尿科醫師、臨床腫瘤科醫師與專科護理師在場；第 1.5.7 條要求談的內容包含「有限的證據無法判定手術與合併增敏劑的放療哪一個療效較好」，以及兩邊對性功能、腸道功能的影響與治療本身造成死亡的風險。再下面列出三份文件共通的只有三件事：多專科團隊、共同決策，以及不可以只給放療（AUA 的條文寫成「clinicians should not offer radiation therapy alone as a curative treatment」）。圖末列出兩句不准的讀法：「只要不想開刀就可以做」與「我自己對照一下就知道」，並寫明這不是可以自己打勾的檢核表——腫瘤條件之外還有腎功能能不能撐化療、膀胱功能、以及刮不刮得乾淨，這些要看報告與膀胱鏡才知道；最後一句是：三份指引的措辭不一樣，這不是筆誤，把你的腫瘤條件拿去問，我符合的是你手上哪一份指引的哪幾條。
en_alt: Schematic setting the three guidelines' wording on who is suitable for trimodality therapy side by side as one table: three columns for EAU 2026, AUA/ASCO/SUO 2024 and NICE NG2, and six rows for number of tumours and stage, carcinoma in situ, hydronephrosis, resection, bladder function and histological subtype. The figure first states the shape of the evidence: comparing trimodality therapy with radical cystectomy there is no successfully completed randomised trial, the trial that closed for insufficient accrual was SPARE with only 45 patients, and so the criteria in the table are guideline wording rather than thresholds calculated from a randomised trial. The EAU column quotes verbatim: for number and stage "solitary, unifocal cT2-T3a tumours"; for carcinoma in situ "absence of extensive or multifocal CIS"; for hydronephrosis "no or unilateral hydronephrosis"; for resection, that as much visible tumour as possible should be resected and that on a second resection more than half of cases turn out to have residual disease; for bladder function "good baseline bladder function"; and for histological subtype that urothelial carcinoma with squamous, glandular or micropapillary differentiation may be considered while pure squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma should be advised surgery instead. The same EAU paragraph adds that patient selection is the key to good outcomes. The AUA column quotes verbatim: "Patients with large tumors unable to be resected by TURBT, multifocal CIS, T3/T4 tumors, and/or hydronephrosis are not ideal candidates for any type of bladder preserving therapy."; the ideal candidate for carcinoma in situ is written as "no CIS" with random biopsies advised to confirm it; hydronephrosis is written as "no hydronephrosis" with no sentence allowing a unilateral one; resection is written as "complete resection is feasible", with statement 22 asking for a maximal debulking resection; and on histological subtype, adenocarcinoma, sarcoma and squamous cell carcinoma were not included in any prospective radiation-based bladder preservation study. The AUA bladder-function cell is drawn as a dash, with a note that a dash means this figure did not take a corresponding wording from that document, not that the guideline has no view on the item. The whole NICE NG2 column is drawn empty with a hatched fill and labelled: this column is empty, NICE NG2 gives no tumour criteria at all, and nothing was left out or is still being looked up. Below the table a separate box records that what NICE gives is a process rather than tumour criteria: 1.5.5 "Offer a choice of radical cystectomy or radiotherapy with a radiosensitiser"; 1.5.6 requires a urological surgeon who performs radical cystectomy, a clinical oncologist and a clinical nurse specialist to be part of the discussion; and 1.5.7 requires the discussion to cover that the limited evidence cannot establish whether surgery or radiotherapy with a radiosensitiser gives the better outcome, along with the effects of each on sexual and bowel function and the risk of death from the treatment itself. Below that, only three things are common to all three documents: a multidisciplinary team, shared decision-making, and that radiotherapy alone is not an option, the AUA statement reading "clinicians should not offer radiation therapy alone as a curative treatment". The figure closes with two readings it must not be given - "anyone who would rather not have surgery can have this" and "I can check myself against this" - stating that this is not a tick-box list, that beyond the tumour criteria there is whether the kidneys can carry the chemotherapy, bladder function and whether the resection can be complete, none of which can be read off without the reports and a cystoscopy, and that the three guidelines are worded differently and that is not a slip, so take your own tumour details and ask which clauses of which guideline you meet.

zh_alt: 示意圖，分成上下兩層，中間一條斷掉的箭頭。圖上蓋著查證日期 2026-09-13：藥證與給付條文都停在這一天。上層「指引與藥證：換了」有三張卡。第一張是 EV-302／KEYNOTE-A39，第一線、隨機第三期、全球開放標示，未曾接受全身治療的局部晚期或轉移性泌尿道上皮癌 886 人（enfortumab vedotin 加 pembrolizumab 442、化療 444）；註冊那一版中位追蹤 17.2 個月，中位總存活 31.5 對 16.1 個月，風險比 0.47（0.38 到 0.58）；2.5 年追蹤的更新分析，中位總存活 33.8 個月（95% 信賴區間 26.1 到 39.3）對 15.9（13.6 到 18.3），風險比 0.51（0.43 到 0.61），中位無惡化存活 12.5 對 6.3 個月，風險比 0.48（0.41 到 0.57）；兩組數字都對但不可混用，追蹤拉長之後中位數往上、風險比也往上，這是正常行為。同一張卡裡放反應率：確認的客觀反應率 67.7%（63.1 到 72.1）對 44.4%（39.7 到 49.2），分母是基準時有可測量病灶的人 437 對 441；完全反應率 29.1% 對 12.5%；並標明反應率不是治癒率、完全反應不等於治癒，整群人的中位總存活仍然是 33.8 個月，以及周邊神經病變在有結果紀錄的 373 人中只有 13% 完全恢復、87% 仍有殘留。第二張卡是用不了那個組合的人還有兩條有隨機證據的路：JAVELIN Bladder 100，含鉑化療四到六個療程後未惡化的 700 人，一年存活率 71.3% 對 58.4%，中位總存活 21.4 對 14.3 個月，風險比 0.69（0.56 到 0.86），第 3 級以上不良事件 47.4% 對 25.2%，並列出誰不適用；CheckMate 901，只收適合 cisplatin 的 608 人，中位追蹤 33.6 個月，中位總存活 21.7 對 18.9 個月，風險比 0.78（0.63 到 0.96），P 等於 0.02，完全反應 21.7% 對 11.8%，完全反應中位持續 37.1 對 13.2 個月，第 3 級以上不良事件 61.8% 對 51.7%，對照組只有 9% 接受 avelumab 維持。第三張卡是台灣藥證：食藥署許可證 衛部菌疫輸字第001212號（enfortumab vedotin），異動日 2026-05-08，適應症已登載「併用 pembrolizumab 適用於治療局部晚期或轉移性泌尿道上皮癌（mUC）的成人病人」；藥證是可以上市的資格，不等於健保付錢。兩層之間的斷箭頭寫著「藥證有，健保沒有」。下層「台灣健保：沒換」也有三張卡。第一張是 9.109 enfortumab vedotin，113 年 5 月 1 日生效，標第三線、單用、一生六個療程，條文逐字為適用於先前接受過含鉑化學治療、後續接受免疫檢查點抑制劑治療失敗後疾病惡化的局部晚期或轉移性泌尿道上皮癌成人病人，以及每位病人限給付6個療程；對應的證據是 EV-301，608 人，中位總存活 12.88 對 8.97 個月，風險比 0.70（0.56 到 0.89）。第二張是 9.69 有付的另外兩格：nivolumab 與 cisplatin 及 gemcitabine 併用至多 6 個療程、接續單用 nivolumab 做為第一線治療，並要求腎絲球過濾率 60 以上；avelumab 維持限 4 至 6 個療程後疾病未惡化且達部分緩解或疾病穩定者，並標明 JAVELIN Bladder 100 收的是沒有惡化、包含完全緩解，兩邊照原文並陳。第三張卡畫成一個虛線空框，框裡只有「零筆」兩個字：第一線 enfortumab vedotin 併用 pembrolizumab 的給付條文全文檔搜尋零筆；零筆的意思是查不到列項，不是確定不給付，也不是所以只能自費，要問醫務課；圖上不寫任何金額。最後一欄寫這一頁的有效期停在 2026-09-13，不要拿它當今天的規則用，也不要憑它自行停藥或改療程。
en_alt: Schematic in two stacked layers with a broken arrow between them. The figure is stamped with the verification date 2026-09-13; every licence and reimbursement clause stops on that date. The top layer, "guidelines and the marketing licence: changed", holds three cards. The first is EV-302 / KEYNOTE-A39, first line, randomised phase III, global and open label, in 886 patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab 442, chemotherapy 444). The registration analysis, median follow-up 17.2 months, gave median overall survival 31.5 vs 16.1 months, hazard ratio 0.47 (0.38 to 0.58); the 2.5-year update gave 33.8 months (95% confidence interval 26.1 to 39.3) vs 15.9 (13.6 to 18.3), hazard ratio 0.51 (0.43 to 0.61), and median progression-free survival 12.5 vs 6.3 months, hazard ratio 0.48 (0.41 to 0.57). Both sets are correct but must not be mixed; with longer follow-up the medians rise and so does the hazard ratio. The same card carries the response rates: confirmed objective response 67.7% (63.1 to 72.1) vs 44.4% (39.7 to 49.2) in the 437 and 441 patients with measurable disease at baseline, and complete response 29.1% vs 12.5%, with the warning that a response rate is not a cure rate, that a complete response is not a cure because the median overall survival of the whole population is still 33.8 months, and that of the 373 patients with a recorded outcome peripheral neuropathy resolved completely in 13% while 87% still had residual neuropathy at the last assessment. The second card holds the two roads with randomised evidence for those who cannot have that combination: JAVELIN Bladder 100, 700 patients without progression after four to six cycles of platinum chemotherapy, one-year survival 71.3% vs 58.4%, median overall survival 21.4 vs 14.3 months, hazard ratio 0.69 (0.56 to 0.86), grade 3 or above adverse events 47.4% vs 25.2%, with the list of who it does not apply to; and CheckMate 901, 608 patients fit for cisplatin, median follow-up 33.6 months, median overall survival 21.7 vs 18.9 months, hazard ratio 0.78 (0.63 to 0.96), P=0.02, complete response 21.7% vs 11.8%, median duration of complete response 37.1 vs 13.2 months, grade 3 or above adverse events 61.8% vs 51.7%, and only 9% of the control arm on avelumab maintenance. The third card is the Taiwanese licence: TFDA licence number 001212 for enfortumab vedotin, amended 2026-05-08, now registered for use in combination with pembrolizumab in adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma. A licence is permission to sell, not a decision to pay. The broken arrow between the layers reads "the licence exists; the reimbursement does not". The bottom layer, "Taiwan National Health Insurance: unchanged", holds three cards. The first is clause 9.109 for enfortumab vedotin, in force from 1 May 2024, labelled third line, monotherapy and six cycles per lifetime, with the clause quoted verbatim and the lifetime ceiling of 6 cycles; the evidence behind it is EV-301, 608 patients, median overall survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months, hazard ratio 0.70 (0.56 to 0.89). The second is clause 9.69 and the two cells that are paid for: nivolumab with cisplatin and gemcitabine for up to 6 cycles followed by nivolumab alone as first-line treatment, requiring a glomerular filtration rate of 60 or above; and avelumab maintenance after 4 to 6 cycles without progression in partial response or stable disease, noting that JAVELIN Bladder 100 enrolled patients without progression, which includes a complete response. The third card is drawn as an empty dashed box containing only the words "zero hits": a full-text search of the regulations for first-line enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab returns nothing, which means no entry was found rather than "not reimbursed" or "so you must pay yourself" - ask the medical affairs office. No price appears anywhere. The closing band states that this page stops on 2026-09-13, should not be used as today's rule, and must not be used to stop or change any treatment.
