en_alt: Schematic in three blocks. The first block draws two rows of ten cells: the Taiwan row has three cells filled and a fourth drawn as a dashed hatched outline, carrying "for every ten urothelial carcinoma registrations in Taiwan, three to four are in the upper tract"; the Western row has one cell filled and a second hatched, carrying "one to two in ten". The basis is printed underneath: Taiwan Cancer Registry long-term trend file, diagnosis year 2023, invasive-only basis, bladder cancer 2,562 cases and cancer of the renal pelvis and other urinary organs 1,884 cases, the latter 42.4% of the two added together; the EAU 2025 upper tract guideline states 5% to 10% of all urothelial carcinomas; and the file's own note that these are invasive cancer incidence data age-standardised to the 2000 world standard population. Three red caveat boxes sit alongside: first, the numerator is formally "cancer of the renal pelvis and other urinary organs", ICD-9 189.1 to 189.9, which includes the urethra and other unspecified urinary organs and is not purely upper tract; second, the denominator is invasive-only and excludes bladder carcinoma in situ, so putting carcinoma in situ back into the denominator lowers the proportion; third, Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Volume XI does not include Taiwan, so there is no international ranking on the same basis. A band then states the two sentences that are never written: never "the highest in the world", because that is a sentence recurring in the literature rather than a calculated ranking; and never "half of Taiwan's cases", because the 42.4% is biased at both ends. Two notes follow: the Western 5% to 10% is itself moving - the Norwegian national registry, 1999 to 2018, 3,096 patients, put the upper tract at 11.8% of all urothelial carcinoma, rising from 9.9% to 12.8%, and the Dutch national registry, 1993 to 2017, 13,314 patients, saw the age-standardised incidence rise from 2.0 to 3.2 per 100,000; and in the Taiwanese upper-tract group women outnumber men, 1,090 women and 794 men in 2023. The second block holds three announcement cards under a band reading "the same day, two different document numbers". On 4 November 2003, document number 0920002350 banned five aristolochic acid-containing herbal materials - Guang Fang Ji, Qing Mu Xiang, Guan Mu Tong, Ma Dou Ling and Tian Xian Teng - from manufacture, dispensing, import, export or sale from the date of the announcement. On the same day, document number 0920002349 also banned preparations containing those five materials from manufacture and import and revoked their product licences. The third card is drawn in a different colour and labelled "NOT in the ban": on 27 February 2004, document number 0930000756 set the management regulation for asarum - the part used changes from the whole plant to the root, concentrated preparations must be made by decoction in water, and finished products may only be sold after passing the established HPLC test, with any marketed asarum product found to contain aristolochic acid dealt with under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. A closing line notes that asarum was not banned; the part used, the process and the testing were changed. The third block holds two analysis cards pointing opposite ways. On the left, a downward arrow: Scientific Reports 2019, an interrupted time series of the Taiwan Cancer Registry from 1995 to 2013, in which the slope for cancer of the renal pelvis and other urinary organs turned at 2000 and again at 2011 and fell by 3.4% per year after the second join point, with the authors writing "possibly associated with". On the right, an upward arrow: J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2023, the same registry from 2001 to 2018, in which the incidence of upper tract urothelial carcinoma rose significantly, average annual percentage change +1.47% (95% confidence interval 1.03 to 1.90, p less than 0.001). The closing band reads "the same registry, two analyses with opposite conclusions", and adds the two directions in the trend file itself: the age-standardised rate peaked in 2010 at 4.93 and was 3.91 in 2023, while the case count rose from 1,505 to 1,884 over the same period. By rate it is drifting down; by number of people it is still going up, so "the ban brought it down" is not written.

zh_alt: 示意圖，兩欄並排，中間畫一條虛線分隔並標明「這兩欄的證據強度不一樣」。最上方一條橫幅寫著：風險因子是流行病學在一大群人身上算出來的統計，不是任何一個人的過錯。左欄「發生率：證據很硬」有四張卡。第一張放三份獨立研究：89 篇觀察性研究、57,145 例膀胱癌的統合分析，目前吸菸者合併勝算比 3.14（95% 信賴區間 2.53 到 3.75）、曾吸菸者 1.83（1.52 到 2.14），並標明勝算比是兩組「有比沒有」的比值、不是機率差幾倍，所以同框放絕對數字；NIH-AARP 前瞻世代（男 281,394 人、女 186,134 人，451.9 萬人年）的每十萬人年發生率長條：從不吸菸 39.8、曾吸菸 119.8（風險比 2.22）、目前吸菸 177.3（風險比 4.06，3.66 到 4.50）；第三份是 83 篇膀胱癌研究的統合分析，相對風險所有吸菸者 2.58、目前吸菸 3.47、曾吸菸 2.04。第二張卡：量與年數有關係但不是等比例——強度在一天 15 支、累積量在 50 包-年之後出現高原，開始吸菸的年齡越小風險越高；戒菸效益 from 20 years before diagnosis 最明顯，而且即使戒了很久，風險也不會回到從不吸菸的水準，但這不是「戒了也沒用」的意思。第三張卡：族群可歸因分率是族群層次的估計、不是任何一個人身上的判決，歐洲男性 43%、女性 26%，美國那個世代男性 0.50、女性 0.52，不同族群不同年代不要互換；並標明台灣自己的可歸因比例查不到任何本土估計。第四張卡是上泌尿道那一邊的另一組數字：歐洲泌尿科醫學會 2025 年上泌尿道指引寫菸品暴露讓相對風險上升 2.5 到 7.0 倍，29 國 101 個中心 2,380 人的登記裡 53.3% 是曾吸菸或目前吸菸；但高雄與弘前的對照世代（台灣 765 人對日本 325 人）裡，台灣病人的抽菸史比日本病人少，p 小於 0.001。右欄「確診之後戒菸與復發：這一格的證據是空的」有四張卡。第一張是只有一顆點的森林圖：復發的合併次分布風險比 0.99（95% 信賴區間 0.61 到 1.61），虛線標 1.0；族群標籤是到 2022 年 1 月為止只找到 9 篇合格文獻、約 5,500 位膀胱癌病人，絕大多數是非肌肉侵犯型，只有 1 篇含肌肉侵犯型；總存活、癌症特異存活與無惡化存活各只有 3 篇，結果互相衝突。第二張卡用大字寫「只有 25 人（14%）戒掉」：英國 BCPP 研究收 722 位非肌肉侵犯型病人（pTa、pT1、原位癌），中位追蹤 4.21 年，戒菸與復發風險無關（p=0.352），作者自己的結論是戒菸人數太少、這份研究回答不了這個問題。接著一條紅框橫幅：這一格的證據是空的——不是「戒菸沒有用」，也不是「戒菸會讓它不復發」。第三張卡並排放兩句指引原文：歐洲泌尿科醫學會 2026 年非肌肉侵犯型指引仍寫 smoking increases the risk of tumour recurrence and progression in NMIBC patients，但建議條文只有一句 Counsel smokers to stop smoking，理由明寫是抽菸對整體健康的危害。第四張卡是證據正向的那一格：密集戒菸方案戒掉 36%、標準衛教 6%，能不能戒得掉跟有沒有人陪著戒有關係，不在意志力。兩欄之間與下方的分隔說明寫著：左欄是三份獨立的大型研究、方向一致、落在同一個數量級；右欄合起來只有 9 篇、約 5,500 人，合併之後看不出差別，唯一的前瞻世代只有 25 人戒掉；左欄的數字不可以搬到右欄，右欄的空白也不可以被讀成「戒菸沒有用」。最下方另有一格疾病特異死亡：同一份 83 篇統合分析的相對風險，所有吸菸者 1.47（1.24 到 1.75）、目前吸菸 1.53（1.12 到 2.09）、曾吸菸 1.44（0.99 到 2.11，信賴區間跨過 1）；已經戒掉的人估計值落在中間而且統計上不確定，這是誠實的形狀，不是好消息也不是壞消息。
en_alt: Schematic in two columns with a dashed rule between them labelled "these two columns do not carry the same weight of evidence". A band across the top reads: a risk factor is a statistic calculated across a very large group of people; it is not anyone's fault. The left column, "incidence: the evidence is strong", holds four cards. The first carries three independent studies: a meta-analysis of 89 observational studies and 57,145 bladder cancers, giving a pooled odds ratio of 3.14 (95% confidence interval 2.53 to 3.75) for current smokers and 1.83 (1.52 to 2.14) for former smokers, with the note that an odds ratio is not a multiple of a probability, which is why the absolute rates sit in the same frame; bars for the NIH-AARP prospective cohort (281,394 men, 186,134 women, 4.519 million person-years) showing 39.8 per 100,000 person-years in never-smokers, 119.8 in former smokers (hazard ratio 2.22) and 177.3 in current smokers (hazard ratio 4.06, 3.66 to 4.50); and a meta-analysis of 83 studies giving relative risks of 2.58 for all smokers, 3.47 for current smokers and 2.04 for former smokers. The second card: amount and duration matter but not in proportion - intensity plateaus beyond 15 cigarettes a day and cumulative exposure beyond 50 pack-years, the younger someone starts the higher the risk, cessation is most beneficial "from 20 years before diagnosis", and even after long-term cessation an elevated risk remains, which does not mean quitting is pointless. The third card: the population attributable fraction is an estimate at population level and not a verdict on any one person - 43% in European men and 26% in European women, 0.50 in men and 0.52 in women in the American cohort, not to be swapped between populations or eras; and no local Taiwanese estimate could be found. The fourth card is the separate set of upper-tract figures: the EAU 2025 upper tract guideline puts the relative risk increase at 2.5 to 7.0 fold, and in a registry of 2,380 patients across 29 countries and 101 centres 53.3% were former or current smokers; but in a comparison cohort from Kaohsiung and Hirosaki (765 Taiwanese vs 325 Japanese patients) the Taiwanese patients had less smoking history, p less than 0.001. The right column, "stopping smoking after diagnosis and recurrence: this cell is empty", holds four cards. The first is a forest plot with a single point: pooled sub-distribution hazard ratio for recurrence 0.99 (95% confidence interval 0.61 to 1.61), with the null line at 1.0; the population label records that up to January 2022 only 9 eligible studies covering about 5,500 bladder cancer patients were found, the great majority non-muscle-invasive with only 1 study including muscle-invasive disease, and that overall survival, cancer-specific survival and progression-free survival had 3 studies each with conflicting results. The second card carries in large type "only 25 (14%) stopped": the British BCPP study enrolled 722 patients with non-muscle-invasive disease (pTa, pT1, CIS), median follow-up 4.21 years, cessation was unrelated to recurrence risk (p=0.352), and the authors concluded that too few people stopped for the study to answer the question. A red band follows: the evidence in this cell is empty - not "stopping smoking does not help", and not "stopping smoking keeps it from coming back". The third card sets two guideline sentences side by side: the EAU 2026 non-muscle-invasive guideline still states that smoking increases the risk of tumour recurrence and progression in NMIBC patients, while its recommendation is the single line "counsel smokers to stop smoking", given for the general health risks of tobacco smoking. The fourth card is the cell where the evidence is positive: an intensive cessation programme achieved 36% cessation against 6% with standard advice, and whether someone manages to stop depends on whether anyone is alongside them rather than on willpower. The divider text states that the left column is three independent large studies, consistent in direction and on the same order of magnitude, while the right column is 9 studies and about 5,500 people showing no difference when pooled, with only 25 people who stopped in the single prospective cohort; the left column's figures may not be carried into the right column, and the right column's emptiness may not be read as "stopping smoking does not help". A final cell below covers disease-specific mortality from the same meta-analysis of 83 studies: relative risk 1.47 (1.24 to 1.75) for all smokers, 1.53 (1.12 to 2.09) for current smokers and 1.44 (0.99 to 2.11, the confidence interval crossing 1) for former smokers; for those who have already stopped the estimate sits between the two and is statistically uncertain, which is an honest shape and neither good news nor bad news.

sources: E[E-S36] van Osch FHM, Jochems SHJ, van Schooten F-J, Bryan RT, Zeegers MP. Quantified relations between exposure to tobacco smoking and bladder cancer risk: a meta-analysis of 89 observational studies. Int J Epidemiol. 2016;45(3):857-870 - 57,145 bladder cancers; current smokers OR 3.14 (2.53-3.75), former 1.83 (1.52-2.14); plateau at 15 cigarettes a day and 50 pack-years; cessation most beneficial "from 20 years before diagnosis" and an elevated risk remains after long-term cessation; European population attributable fraction 43% in men and 26% in women

E[E-S37] Freedman ND, Silverman DT, Hollenbeck AR, Schatzkin A, Abnet CC. Association between smoking and risk of bladder cancer among men and women. JAMA. 2011;306(7):737-745 - NIH-AARP, 281,394 men and 186,134 women, 4.519 million person-years; 39.8 / 119.8 / 177.3 per 100,000 person-years, HR 2.22 and 4.06 (3.66-4.50); attributable fraction 0.50 in men and 0.52 in women

E[E-S38] Cumberbatch MG, Rota M, Catto JWF, La Vecchia C. The Role of Tobacco Smoke in Bladder and Kidney Carcinogenesis. Eur Urol. 2016;70(3):458-466 - 83 bladder cancer studies; incidence RR 2.58 / 3.47 / 2.04; disease-specific mortality RR 1.47 (1.24-1.75), 1.53 (1.12-2.09) and 1.44 (0.99-2.11, crossing 1)

E[E-S39] Caini S, Del Riccio M, Vettori V, et al. Prognostic Impact of Post-Diagnosis Smoking Cessation among Bladder Cancer Patients: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis. Cancers. 2022;14(16):4022 - 9 eligible studies to January 2022, about 5,500 patients, mostly non-muscle-invasive with only 1 including muscle-invasive disease; recurrence SHR 0.99 (0.61-1.61); 3 studies each for overall, cancer-specific and progression-free survival, conflicting

E[E-S40] van Osch FHM, Jochems SHJ, Reulen RC, et al. The association between smoking cessation before and after diagnosis and non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer recurrence: a prospective cohort study. Cancer Causes Control. 2018;29(7):675-683 - BCPP, 722 patients (pTa, pT1, CIS), median follow-up 4.21 years, only 25 (14%) of smokers stopped, p=0.352

E[E-S41] EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer - "smoking increases the risk of tumour recurrence and progression in NMIBC patients" beside the single recommendation "Counsel smokers to stop smoking", given for general health risks; and the randomised intensive cessation programme, 36% vs 6%

E[E-S1] Masson-Lecomte A, Gontero P, Birtle A, et al. EAU Guidelines on Upper Urinary Tract Urothelial Carcinoma (2025) - tobacco exposure increases the relative risk of upper tract urothelial carcinoma 2.5 to 7.0 fold; 53.3% ever or current smokers in a registry of 2,380 patients across 29 countries and 101 centres

E[E-S23] Luo H-L, Ohyama C, Hatakeyama S, et al. Unusual presentation of upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma in Taiwan: Direct comparison from Taiwan-Japan UTUC Collaboration Cohort. Int J Urol. 2020;27(4):327-332 - Kaohsiung 765 vs Hirosaki 325, less smoking history in the Taiwanese patients, p<0.001
